messages:
newhire_zoe: Hey team — first day! Quick weirdness: I installed Miniforge (conda) because I need some scientific wheels, and also followed the onboarding to install asdf. `asdf global python 3.11.6` but running `which python` still points to conda's python. pipx installs are ending up under conda envs and Poetry seems to pick the wrong interpreter. Help? Should I use conda only for data repos and asdf for everything else? Any minimal zsh snippet to keep things sane?

marcus: welcome Zoe! We don't ban conda but we try to avoid having base conda active by default. Run `conda config --set auto_activate_base false` so conda doesn't hijack PATH. Put asdf init ahead of conda in your zprofile so shims win. Example minimal zprofile:
```bash
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$PATH
. "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh" || true
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
# enable conda but don't auto-activate base
if [ -f "$HOME/miniforge3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh" ]; then . "$HOME/miniforge3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh"; fi
```
That keeps asdf-managed python first and still lets you `conda activate` per-project.

devx_anya: +1. For pipx: install pipx into the asdf python (the one asdf points to) so `pipx ensurepath` puts binaries in $HOME/.local/bin. Avoid installing pipx into conda base. For Poetry we recommend the asdf poetry plugin or installing poetry into the asdf python per-project (`python -m pip install --user poetry`) and use `poetry env use $(asdf which python)` inside repos if needed.

infra-bot: Dev env doc: <internal/dev-setup/conda-asdf.md> has recommended snippets and a note about `conda init` vs `conda.sh` sourcing. Also see <internal/dev-setup/pipx-poetry.md> for installing CLI tools.

priya: direnv tip: if you have projects using conda, your .envrc can call `layout_conda` or `conda activate <env>` explicitly. We prefer repo-local activation and not auto-activating base. Example .envrc snippet we use: `use asdf && watch_file .tool-versions && layout python` or if using conda `source ~/.local/share/conda/conda.sh && conda activate myenv`. Remember to `direnv allow` after editing.

newhire_zoe: great — that explains a lot. One follow-up: I have an existing ~/.zshrc that runs `conda init` which appends stuff and auto-activates base. Should I undo that?

marcus: yes undo `conda init` changes (remove the auto-activation bits) and prefer explicit sourcing of `conda.sh` as in the snippet. `conda init` tends to put hook code in zshrc that causes base to come first. If you want I can paste a small cleanup diff.

devx_anya: and run `which -a python` after the changes — you should see the asdf shim (`~/.asdf/shims/python`) before any conda paths. If not, post `echo $PATH` and `which -a python pipx` and we can eyeball it.

newhire_zoe: thanks all! I'll update zprofile, disable auto_activate_base, reinstall pipx into asdf python, and try direnv per-repo. I'll ping with outputs if anything still acts up. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
